answer.book: Othonis Casmanni Nucleus mysteriorum naturae enucleatus (Hamburg 1605), a Latin physiology in two books (Liber primus and Liber secundus; the printed table calls them Pars I and Pars II), preceded by a dedication, a preface and a table of chapters, with chapters numbered within each book and Liber secundus divided into sections in its chapter on the bones.
